title: Time intervals & timetables
examples: How do I find the time between two events?
Can you show me how to read a train schedule?
What does the time difference mean?

explain.say: Today we will learn about time intervals. A time interval is the time between two moments.

draw.text: Time Intervals: Time between two points

explain.say: Imagine a movie starts at two o'clock. It finishes at two thirty. We need to find the time between these two times.
You can count the time forward from the start time. From two o'clock to two thirty is thirty minutes.
Next we look at timetables. A timetable shows when things happen over time. Look at this bus schedule.
The bus leaves at nine fifteen. The next one leaves at nine forty-five. We need to find the time between these two times.

faq.q: How do I find the time between two times?
faq.a: You can count the time forward from the earlier time to the later time. For example, from one o'clock to one thirty is thirty minutes.
asks: How long is it from 1:00 to 1:30?

faq.a: A timetable is a chart that shows scheduled times for events. It helps us know when things will start and finish.

faq.q: If a train leaves at ten o'clock and the journey is thirty minutes, when does it arrive?
faq.a: You add the journey time to the starting time. Ten o'clock plus thirty minutes equals ten thirty.
asks: When does the train get there?

faq.q: Do I need to know the minutes when reading a timetable?
faq.a: Yes, you must read the minutes carefully. The minutes tell you exactly where in the hour the event happens.
asks: Should I look at the minutes?

faq.q: What if the time crosses the hour mark?
faq.a: If you cross the hour, you can count up to the next full hour first. Then count the remaining minutes.
asks: What if it goes past the hour?
How do I handle crossing the hour?

facts: Time intervals measure the duration between two points in time.
Timetables show scheduled times for services like buses or trains.
Minutes are used to measure parts of an hour.
To find the duration, you subtract the start time from the end time.

quiz.say: A class starts at one ten and ends at one forty. What is the time interval?
quiz.why: You count from ten minutes past the hour to forty minutes past the hour, which is thirty minutes.

wrong.0: This is too much time; you only moved within the same hour.
wrong.1: You counted the end time instead of the difference.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you subtract ten from forty.

quiz.say: A film starts at two fifteen and runs for an hour. What time does it finish?
quiz.why: Adding one full hour to two fifteen brings you exactly to three fifteen.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you only add the minutes.
wrong.2: You should be adding the time, not subtracting it.
wrong.3: You mixed up the numbers and added them together incorrectly.

quiz.say: A train leaves at eight forty and arrives at nine ten. What is the journey time?
quiz.why: From eight forty to nine o'clock is twenty minutes, and then ten more minutes makes thirty minutes.

wrong.0: You added the minutes incorrectly instead of counting the gap.
wrong.1: You counted the time from eight o'clock, not eight forty.
wrong.3: This is too long; you only moved a little bit past the hour.
